classes.name: Perch-Gley Pallic
classes.description: Perch-Gley Pallic Soils are slowly permeable with near surface waterlogging.
classes.orderDescription: Pallic soils typically have pale subsoils with little iron oxide, weak soil structure and dense subsurface layers. They commonly become wet in winter and dry in summer, and are associated with loess deposits in eastern New Zealand and Manawatū.

source.title: Manaaki Whenua Fundamental Soil Layer (FSL) — NZ Soil Classification
source.dateNote: Legacy mapping: source surveys vary from the 1960s to 2000. The WMS layer metadata lists publication in 2011. Not a current soil test.
source.scaleNote: Regional mapping at about 1:50,000. The 10 m app lookup grid is for display only and does not imply 10 m soil accuracy.

source.coverageNote: All 14 source polygons intersecting the map extent have the same mapped group: Perch-Gley Pallic (PP). The overlay covers the entire map extent. This coarse classification does not describe every paddock or soil variation on site.
source.processing: WMS map image is unchanged in geographic content and re-encoded losslessly. Class lookup sampled from the complete-coverage image to 256×250 cells, north-to-south, using the verified PP palette. WFS feature attributes and six GetFeatureInfo queries independently verify the group. Source polygons are retained in optional GeoJSON; their original extents extend outside the farm context.
limitations: This is the legacy FSL classification, not S-map.
No pH, nutrient, rooting-depth or water-capacity values are provided by this particular service layer.
Group descriptions are general mapped soil characteristics, not a measurement or recommendation for an individual paddock.
